name: Seconds to Minutes Conversion
description: Construct a program that obtains minutes and remaining seconds from the input amount of time in seconds. For example, 500 seconds contains 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

comments.content: We need to read and process the value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the seconds.
We need to read the seconds that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the seconds by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

To obtain the minutes in seconds, we divide the seconds by 60 because there are 60 seconds in a minute. Note that since both operands of division operator are integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.

To obtain the remaining seconds after taking away the minutes, we have to take the remainder of the seconds divided by 60. This is because there are 60 seconds in a minute. Note that the % operator returns the remainder of the division.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the minutes and remaining seconds from the input amount of time in seconds. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given strings and value of the variables.
